title: The King's Backup Elephants
body: In medieval Spain, the chess piece we now call the bishop was known as an elephant. King Alfonso wrote that real kings always took at least two of these giant animals into battle. That way, if one elephant got hurt, the king would always have a backup ready to fight.

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, the bishop on the chessboard was carved to look like a quiet, powerful elephant. A wise king named Alfonso wrote that a ruler should never travel to war with just one of these gentle giants. If one became too tired or hurt, there would always be a second companion ready to help protect the kingdom.
variants.luca: King Alfonso had a brilliant battle plan: never charge into a fight with only one giant war elephant! He insisted on bringing a pair of these massive beasts to charge across the board. That way, if your first heavy hitter got knocked out, the backup elephant could stampede right in to save the day.
variants.cn: 很久以前，在西班牙，棋盘上的“象”真的被雕成了大象的样子——安静又有力气的大块头。聪明的阿方索国王在书里写道：国王出门打仗，千万不能只带一头大象。万一这头大象累了、受伤了，旁边还有第二个伙伴，随时准备顶上来，保护整个王国。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
